newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Pacific Retail wants to spread its wings.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Retail wants to spread its wings.

text.p: Pacific Retail Group will soon offer financial services, may look to set up shop in Australia, and expects to more than double its pre-tax profit next year, and but current trading conditions are tough, Managing Director Greg Lancaster said on Thursday.
New Zealand's largest retailer of home appliances and consumer electronics plans significant growth, but will struggle to post its forecast NZ$7 million pre-tax profit for the 1996/97 year.
"Christmas hasn't been quite as strong as we'd have liked it to be, so $7 million is going to be a bit of a grunt," Lancaster told Reuters in an interview.
"But we're more focused on 1997/98 because we have been in the midst of acquisitions and mergers and relocating teams of people and so on."

Pacific Retail, formerly Noel Leeming, merged with Bond and Bond late last year. Lancaster said the group's focus this year would be on maximising efficiencies and the group's effectiveness in a depressed market.
"The industry as a whole is not having a very good time. The brown goods side of the industry in particular, as far as we can determine, is not profitable on the supply side," he said.
Although margins had not changed, the high value of the New Zealand dollar had seen increased competition among importing suppliers, resulting in lower wholesale and retail prices.

"If you're making a 20 percent margin and you're selling something for $500 you've made $100 profit, but if you're now selling it for $350, you're making $70, so that's the downside of the exchange rate for this industry," Lancaster said.
While the trough retailers were experiencing would prevail for longer than originally anticipated, Lancaster expected an improvement in the latter part of the year.
And the group's recent securitisation of its hire purchase receivables had opened new doors -- financial services will soon be on the appliance retailer's menu.
"We are looking at providing hire purchase funding and credit administration to other durables retailers to provide us with ongoing growth," Lancaster said.

Pacific Retail, through its finance company Pacific Retail Finance, securitised its hire purchase ledger to achieve a much lower cost of funds and to get the receivables off the company's balance sheet.

By doinf so, it made a one-off pre-tax gain of NZ$3 million and through cheaper funding costs secured an ongoing annual lift of $2.3 million to pre-tax profit, which it expects to grow as more paper is added to the book.
Now Pacific wants to offer the same service to other retailers, and sees substantial potential to generate new revenue streams in the process.
"It would have the potential to increase the size of the finance company by 50 percent plus over time," Lancaster said.

He said Pacific Retail's profits would leap in 1997/98 as the benefits of the Bond and Bond merger and the pickup in the retail sector came through. Earlier projections of an $18 million 1997/98 pre-tax profit were still close to the mark, Lancaster said.
"Those projections were done in June and July when the market was easier than it is now, but I still think more than double the $7 million."
At that stage, the group would look to expand.

"My view is that we need to look at some expansion, now whether that be into other forms of durable retailing here, or whether it be into appliance retailing in other markets, it's really too early to say," Lancaster said.
He said Australia was the logical overseas market to look at, although it would not be given serious consideration until late this year or early in 1998.
"A lot's happened in the past wee while, now it's time to get back to running an appliance retail operation," he said.
--Wellington newsroom.
